title: QuickForge Response Atlas — personal proto notes
content:
Goal:
Lightweight authoring surface for engineers/product to describe 'response archetypes' (aka response blueprints) and map them to model variants, cost tiers, and fallback policies.

Why:
- Teams repeatedly craft similar reply patterns (concise answer, long-form explainer, legal-safe summary, quick-fact-check).
- Current approach: ad-hoc prompt templates per service + hand-tuned model selection. Hard to audit / test / route.
- Hypothesis: small structured catalog + runtime bindings reduces variation, makes rollback/fallback easier, and exposes clear telemetry for cost vs quality tradeoffs.

Core idea (working name: QuickForge Response Atlas):
- Author defines an atlas entry: id, short description, intent tags, obligate constraints (latency budget, max tokens, safety filters), preferred model family + fallback chain, and exemplar prompts/test cases.
- Runtime: request arrives with "atlas_id" or inferred archetype -> router picks model variant (cost/latency-aware) + applies template and any post-processing hooks.
- Observability: per-atlas metrics (p50/p95 latency, tokens, cost per call, quality score from eval set, error rate).

Minimal data model (rough):
- atlas_id (string)
- display_name (string)
- intent_tags (list)
- preferred_mode (concise | verbose | structured | code | embed)
- latency_slo_ms (int)
- max_response_tokens (int)
- model_priority_list (ordered list of model refs)
- fallback_policy (e.g., degrade-to-summary, retry-with-simpler-model, return-canned)
- example_prompts (list)
- smoke_tests (ids of eval prompts)

User stories (first pass):
- As a product engineer I want to create a "concise-expert" atlas entry so I can consistently serve short technical answers across products.
- As an SRE I want to route atlas entries with p95 > 600ms to a different pool automatically to preserve global SLOs.
- As a PM I want a report showing cost delta if an atlas switches from model-A-8q to model-B-4q for top 20 queries.
- As QA I want ability to run smoke_tests for an atlas against new model versions before rollout.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UI/CLI to create/edit atlas entry + save to config store (git-backed or DB).
- Runtime honor atlas when atlas_id supplied: model selection + template application + basic fallback.
- Telemetry: per-atlas metrics surfaced in Console (tokens/cost/latency/errors) for last 7 days.
- Smoke-test runner that can execute defined smoke_tests and produce a diff report (tokens, latency, basic correctness heuristics).

UX sketches (notes to self):
- Authoring screen with 3 panels: fields (left), example prompt + live sandbox (center), rollout / traffic split (right).
- Quick 'clone' from existing atlas -> modify constraints and run smoke tests.
- Inline suggestion: recommended quant/variant from Optimize engine (based on token distribution).

Operational considerations:
- Storage: small JSON artifacts per atlas, versioned (we want ability to revert). Suggest storing in a repo + metadata index.
- Rollout: canary percentages, auto-fallback to previous atlas version on regression.
- Security: some atlas entries may reference customer-sensitive prompts — support encryption + KMS scope.
- Multi-tenant: enforce isolation so customer A's atlas does not leak into B.

Telemetry + evals:
- Need per-atlas baseline eval set (smoke_tests) and continuous monitoring against quality regressions.
- Hook into Optimize recommendations: show predicted token savings for quantization changes.
- Define quality metric heuristics for early guardrails: semantic-similarity to reference, hallucination detectors, answer-depth score.

Rollout plan (rapid experiment):
1) Internal-only alpha: implement runtime hook + simple JSON-backed atlas store. Integrate with dev console. (2 sprints)
2) Run with 2 product teams (assistant+help center) for 4 weeks. Capture telemetry, adjust fields.
3) Add smoke-test runner + canary traffic control. (1 sprint)
4) Expand to public beta + docs + onboarding templates.

Open questions / parking lot:
- Who owns the taxonomy of intent_tags? Product taxonomy vs freeform?
- How to best infer atlas_id when none supplied (model-based classifier? heuristics?)
- Do we allow per-atlas custom KVs in session store? Privacy implications.
- Cost accounting: attribute token cost to atlas vs route vs user — need clear rules.
- Interplay with existing rollouts / variant selectors (avoid duplicating config surfaces).

Experiment ideas / quick wins:
- Create 5 canonical atlases (concise-answer, deep-explain, code-completion, policy-safe-summary, instant-embed) and measure percent of traffic that maps to them for one week.
- A/B: for 'concise-answer' run model-A vs model-B for 10% of calls and compute hallucination + satisfaction proxies.
- Auto-suggest atlas during prompt authoring using similarity to atlas example_prompts.

Things to add before moving to PRD:
- Concrete data model fields + JSON schema
- API contract example (HTTP request with atlas_id, sample response envelope)
- RBAC and ownership model for atlas editing
- Example templates for common atlas types (3-5)

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep the initial scope narrow: author + runtime binding + telemetry. Leave fancy inference for later.
- Tie to Optimize: show "estimated savings" during atlas authoring to nudge adoption.
- Reach out to amira + mira for early playtest (pinged them).

Related tickets/places to update:
- JIRA-9876 (proto store)
- CONFLUENCE-1234 (design notes)
- TODO: create GH sketch repo and a demo notebook

Final quick checklist (alpha):
- [ ] JSON schema + migration plan
- [ ] CLI + minimal web UI for authors
- [ ] Runtime hook in router (atlas lookup + apply template)
- [ ] Telemetry wiring to Console + cheap grafana dashboard
- [ ] Smoke-test runner + example evals

-- end --

(rough, half-finished. feel free to steal pieces. will iterate.)
